claim: Intercellular tight junctions form selectively permeable barriers that seal the paracellular space.
source: Intercellular tight junctions form selectively permeable barriers that seal the paracellular space.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about tight junction function.

claim: Trans-tight junction flux has been measured across large epithelial surfaces.
source: Trans-tight junction flux has been measured across large epithelial surfaces, but conductance across individual channels has never been measured.
evidence: This refers to established methods in the field, representing scientific knowledge.

claim: Conductance across individual tight junction channels has never been measured before this study.
source: Trans-tight junction flux has been measured across large epithelial surfaces, but conductance across individual channels has never been measured.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the current work, based on knowledge of the field.

claim: A novel trans-tight junction patch clamp technique can detect flux across individual claudin-2 channels within the tight junction.
source: We report a novel trans-tight junction patch clamp technique that detects flux across individual claudin-2 channels within the tight junction of cultured canine renal tubule or human intestinal epithelial monolayers.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing patch clamp recordings.

claim: Claudin-2 channels display conductances of ~90 pS in both canine renal tubule and human intestinal epithelial cells.
source: In both cells, claudin-2 channels display conductances of ~90 pS.
evidence: This is supported by patch clamp measurements shown in Figures 2 and 5.

claim: Claudin-2 channels are gated.
source: The channels are gated, strictly dependent on claudin-2 expression, and display size- and charge-selectivity typical of claudin-2.
evidence: This is supported by kinetic analyses shown in Figure 3 demonstrating opening and closing events.

claim: Claudin-2 channels are strictly dependent on claudin-2 expression.
source: The channels are gated, strictly dependent on claudin-2 expression, and display size- and charge-selectivity typical of claudin-2.
evidence: This is supported by data showing reduced events in claudin-2 knockdown or absence (Figures 2, 5).

claim: Claudin-2 channels display size- and charge-selectivity typical of claudin-2.
source: The channels are gated, strictly dependent on claudin-2 expression, and display size- and charge-selectivity typical of claudin-2.
evidence: This is supported by biionic potential and dilution potential measurements in Figure 6.

claim: Kinetic analyses indicate claudin-2 channels have one open and two distinct closed states.
source: Kinetic analyses indicate one open and two distinct closed states.
evidence: This is supported by open and closed duration histograms in Figure 3.

claim: Claudin-2 channel conductance is symmetrical and reversible.
source: Conductance is symmetrical and reversible, characteristic of a passive, paracellular process, and blocked by reduced temperature or site-directed mutagenesis and chemical derivatization of the claudin-2 pore.
evidence: This is supported by voltage ramp data in Figure 2 and ionic gradient experiments in Figure 6.

claim: Claudin-2 channel conductance is characteristic of a passive, paracellular process.
source: Conductance is symmetrical and reversible, characteristic of a passive, paracellular process, and blocked by reduced temperature or site-directed mutagenesis and chemical derivatization of the claudin-2 pore.
evidence: This is inferred from the symmetrical behavior and near-zero reversal potential.

claim: Claudin-2 channel conductance is blocked by reduced temperature.
source: Conductance is symmetrical and reversible, characteristic of a passive, paracellular process, and blocked by reduced temperature or site-directed mutagenesis and chemical derivatization of the claudin-2 pore.
evidence: This is supported by temperature reduction experiments shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: Claudin-2 channel conductance is blocked by site-directed mutagenesis and chemical derivatization of the claudin-2 pore.
source: Conductance is symmetrical and reversible, characteristic of a passive, paracellular process, and blocked by reduced temperature or site-directed mutagenesis and chemical derivatization of the claudin-2 pore.
evidence: This is supported by MTSET experiments on claudin-2I66C shown in Figure 7.

claim: Claudin-2 forms gated paracellular channels.
source: We conclude that claudin-2 forms gated paracellular channels and speculate that modulation of tight junction channel gating kinetics may be an unappreciated mechanism of barrier regulation.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all experimental data presented.

claim: Modulation of tight junction channel gating kinetics may be an unappreciated mechanism of barrier regulation.
source: We conclude that claudin-2 forms gated paracellular channels and speculate that modulation of tight junction channel gating kinetics may be an unappreciated mechanism of barrier regulation.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the findings.

claim: Epithelial barriers are essential for the survival of multicellular organisms.
source: Epithelial barriers are essential for the survival of multicellular organisms and allow compartmentalization and controlled interactions between distinct environments (Marchiando et al., 2010, Turner, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Epithelial barriers allow compartmentalization and controlled interactions between distinct environments.
source: Epithelial barriers are essential for the survival of multicellular organisms and allow compartmentalization and controlled interactions between distinct environments (Marchiando et al., 2010, Turner, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Transcellular transport is mediated by proteins that span the plasma membrane.
source: While transcellular transport is mediated by proteins that span the plasma membrane, molecular details of ions, water, and solute transport across the tight junction, i.e. the paracellular path, are less well-defined.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about transcellular transport.

claim: Molecular details of ions, water, and solute transport across the tight junction are less well-defined than transcellular transport.
source: While transcellular transport is mediated by proteins that span the plasma membrane, molecular details of ions, water, and solute transport across the tight junction, i.e. the paracellular path, are less well-defined.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The absence of tools able to detect single channel events at the tight junction has contributed to limited understanding of paracellular transport.
source: This, in part, reflects the absence of tools able to detect single channel events at the tight junction and, therefore, a reliance on methods that measure paracellular flux over large multicellular surfaces (Shen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference about why the field has been limited, supported by citation.

claim: Methods that measure paracellular flux over large multicellular surfaces have limited spatial and temporal resolution.
source: The limited spatial and temporal resolution of these techniques has contributed to the widely held view of tight junction channels as constitutively open and has limited biophysical characterization of these paracellular channels.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of existing methods, based on knowledge of the field.

claim: Limited spatial and temporal resolution of traditional techniques has contributed to the widely held view of tight junction channels as constitutively open.
source: The limited spatial and temporal resolution of these techniques has contributed to the widely held view of tight junction channels as constitutively open and has limited biophysical characterization of these paracellular channels.
evidence: This is an inference about how methodological limitations have shaped scientific understanding.

claim: Paracellular transport is critical to the function of transporting epithelia in many organs.
source: Nevertheless, it is clear that paracellular transport is critical to the function of transporting epithelia in many organs (Bagnat et al., 2007, Simon et al., 1999, Wada et al., 2013) and can be regulated by physiological and pathophysiological stimuli (Heller et al., 2005, Marchiando et al., 2010, Suzuki et al., 2011, Turner et al., 1997, Weber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Paracellular transport can be regulated by physiological and pathophysiological stimuli.
source: Nevertheless, it is clear that paracellular transport is critical to the function of transporting epithelia in many organs (Bagnat et al., 2007, Simon et al., 1999, Wada et al., 2013) and can be regulated by physiological and pathophysiological stimuli (Heller et al., 2005, Marchiando et al., 2010, Suzuki et al., 2011, Turner et al., 1997, Weber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Claudin-2 increases paracellular Na+ conductance.
source: Intestinal epithelial expression of the tight junction protein claudin-2, which increases paracellular Na+ conductance (Amasheh et al., 2002, Wada et al., 2013, Weber et al., 2010), is downregulated after the neonatal period (Holmes et al., 2006) but markedly upregulated in inflammatory and infectious enterocolitis and by several cytokines, including IL-13 (Heller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Intestinal epithelial claudin-2 expression is downregulated after the neonatal period.
source: Intestinal epithelial expression of the tight junction protein claudin-2, which increases paracellular Na+ conductance (Amasheh et al., 2002, Wada et al., 2013, Weber et al., 2010), is downregulated after the neonatal period (Holmes et al., 2006) but markedly upregulated in inflammatory and infectious enterocolitis and by several cytokines, including IL-13 (Heller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Holmes et al., 2006.

claim: Claudin-2 is markedly upregulated in inflammatory and infectious enterocolitis.
source: Intestinal epithelial expression of the tight junction protein claudin-2, which increases paracellular Na+ conductance (Amasheh et al., 2002, Wada et al., 2013, Weber et al., 2010), is downregulated after the neonatal period (Holmes et al., 2006) but markedly upregulated in inflammatory and infectious enterocolitis and by several cytokines, including IL-13 (Heller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Heller et al., 2005.

claim: IL-13 upregulates claudin-2 expression.
source: Intestinal epithelial expression of the tight junction protein claudin-2, which increases paracellular Na+ conductance (Amasheh et al., 2002, Wada et al., 2013, Weber et al., 2010), is downregulated after the neonatal period (Holmes et al., 2006) but markedly upregulated in inflammatory and infectious enterocolitis and by several cytokines, including IL-13 (Heller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Heller et al., 2005.

claim: Claudin-2 upregulation is essential for IL-13-induced increases in paracellular Na+ permeability.
source: This is essential for IL-13-induced increases in paracellular Na+ permeability, as conductance changes are prevented by siRNA-mediated inhibition of claudin-2 upregulation (Weber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Weber et al., 2010.

claim: siRNA-mediated inhibition of claudin-2 upregulation prevents IL-13-induced conductance changes.
source: This is essential for IL-13-induced increases in paracellular Na+ permeability, as conductance changes are prevented by siRNA-mediated inhibition of claudin-2 upregulation (Weber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Weber et al., 2010.

claim: Claudin-2 expression is regulated during development and disease.
source: Thus, claudin-2 expression is regulated during development and disease.
evidence: This is inferred from the previous statements about neonatal downregulation and disease upregulation.

claim: Claudin-2 expression induces large increases in paracellular flux of small cations.
source: Claudin-2 expression induces large increases in paracellular flux of small cations (Amasheh et al., 2002, Furuse et al., 2001, Weber et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: MDCKI monolayers lack endogenous claudin-2 expression.
source: Inducible claudin-2 expression in MDCKI monolayers, which lack endogenous claudin-2 expression, is therefore an ideal experimental model in which to define paracellular, trans-tight junction channels (Angelow and Yu, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation and confirmed by Western blot in Figure 1A.

claim: Inducible claudin-2 expression in MDCKI monolayers is an ideal experimental model to define paracellular, trans-tight junction channels.
source: Inducible claudin-2 expression in MDCKI monolayers, which lack endogenous claudin-2 expression, is therefore an ideal experimental model in which to define paracellular, trans-tight junction channels (Angelow and Yu, 2009).
evidence: This is a claim about the suitability of the model system, supported by citation and inference.

claim: Small amounts of functional claudin-2 were present in MDCKI cells even when expression was repressed.
source: Western blot demonstrated that, relative to the parental MDCKI line, small amounts of functional claudin-2 were present even when expression was repressed, i.e. doxycyline was present, consistent with the known minor leakiness of such regulated expression systems (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1A.

claim: The presence of small amounts of claudin-2 when expression is repressed is consistent with the known minor leakiness of tet-off regulated expression systems.
source: Western blot demonstrated that, relative to the parental MDCKI line, small amounts of functional claudin-2 were present even when expression was repressed, i.e. doxycyline was present, consistent with the known minor leakiness of such regulated expression systems (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on knowledge of tet-off systems and supported by the Western blot data.

claim: MDCKI and MDCKII cells differ primarily in their expression of claudin-2.
source: As expected based on previous comparisons of MDCKI and MDCKII cells (Stevenson et al., 1988), which differ primarily in their expression of claudin-2, induction of claudin-2 expression did not affect tight junction ultrastructure (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Stevenson et al., 1988.

claim: Induction of claudin-2 expression did not affect tight junction ultrastructure.
source: As expected based on previous comparisons of MDCKI and MDCKII cells (Stevenson et al., 1988), which differ primarily in their expression of claudin-2, induction of claudin-2 expression did not affect tight junction ultrastructure (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 1B.

claim: When claudin-2 expression was induced, claudin-2 concentrated at tight junctions and, to a limited extent, in cytoplasmic vesicles.
source: When expression was induced, claudin-2 concentrated at tight junctions and, to a limited extent, in cytoplasmic vesicles (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1C.

claim: Induction of claudin-2 expression reduced transepithelial electrical resistance (TER).
source: Induction of claudin-2 expression also reduced transepithelial electrical resistance (TER; Figure 1D) and increased cationic charge selectivity (Figure 1E) with strict size-selectivity (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by TER measurements shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Induction of claudin-2 expression increased cationic charge selectivity.
source: Induction of claudin-2 expression also reduced transepithelial electrical resistance (TER; Figure 1D) and increased cationic charge selectivity (Figure 1E) with strict size-selectivity (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by PNa+/PCl- measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Claudin-2 expression induces strict size-selectivity.
source: Induction of claudin-2 expression also reduced transepithelial electrical resistance (TER; Figure 1D) and increased cationic charge selectivity (Figure 1E) with strict size-selectivity (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by biionic potential analyses shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Claudin-2 expression induces charge- and size-selective increases in paracellular, trans-tight junction conductance.
source: Claudin-2 expression therefore induces charge- and size-selective increases in paracellular, trans-tight junction conductance.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data in Figure 1.

claim: Measurements of paracellular permeability typically assess relatively large epithelial surfaces and reflect global averages rather than local, site-specific conductances.
source: Measurements of paracellular permeability, such as those above, typically assess relatively large epithelial surfaces and, therefore, reflect global averages rather than local, site-specific conductances.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of traditional methods, based on knowledge of the field.

claim: Scanning and impedance approaches lack the spatial and temporal resolution needed for identification of single channel events.
source: Scanning and impedance approaches have been used in an effort to overcome these limitations (Chen et al., 2013, Gitter et al., 1997, Krug et al., 2009), but these lack the spatial and temporal resolution needed for identification of single channel events.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of alternative methods, supported by citations.

claim: The orientation of trans-tight junction channels between lateral surfaces of two adjacent cells is parallel to plasma membranes.
source: Overall, the greatest obstacle to single channel analyses of tight junction channels has been the orientation of trans-tight junction channels between lateral surfaces of two adjacent cells, i.e. parallel to plasma membranes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a statement about tight junction structure, which is established knowledge and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The orientation of tight junction channels is orthogonal to traditional ion channels and gap junctions.
source: This orientation is orthogonal to traditional ion channels and gap junctions, which cross plasma membranes, and renders most patch clamp techniques unsuitable for measuring trans-tight junction ion flux.
evidence: This is a statement about the structural differences between tight junctions and other channels, based on knowledge.

claim: The orientation of tight junction channels renders most patch clamp techniques unsuitable for measuring trans-tight junction ion flux.
source: This orientation is orthogonal to traditional ion channels and gap junctions, which cross plasma membranes, and renders most patch clamp techniques unsuitable for measuring trans-tight junction ion flux.
evidence: This is an inference about why traditional patch clamp cannot be used, based on structural knowledge.

claim: Conductance events were detected at −100 mV when claudin-2 was expressed.
source: Conductance events detected at −100 mV when claudin-2 was expressed (+Cldn-2).
evidence: This is shown in the patch clamp recording in Figure 2C.

claim: In the absence of induced claudin-2 expression, the frequency of similar sized conductance events was dramatically reduced.
source: In the absence of induced claudin-2 expression (–Cldn-2), the frequency of similar sized conductance events was dramatically reduced.
evidence: This is shown in the patch clamp recording in Figure 2D.

claim: Small claudin-2 independent events were present in parental MDCKI monolayers.
source: Small claudin-2 independent events were present in parental MDCKI monolayers
evidence: This is shown in the patch clamp recording in Figure 2E.

claim: Conductance events were present at +100 mV when claudin-2 was expressed.
source: Conductance events were present at +100 mV when claudin-2 was expressed (+Cldn-2).
evidence: This is shown in the patch clamp recording in Figure 2F.

claim: Events were infrequent in the absence of induced claudin-2 expression at +100 mV.
source: Events were infrequent in the absence of induced claudin-2 expression (–Cldn-2).
evidence: This is shown in the patch clamp recording in Figure 2G.

claim: NPo was reduced by 87% ± 4% at –100 mV after suppression of claudin-2 expression.
source: NPo was reduced by 87% ± 4% (at –100 mV) and 88% ± 6% (at +100 mV) after suppression of claudin-2 expression.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2H.

claim: NPo was reduced by 88% ± 6% at +100 mV after suppression of claudin-2 expression.
source: NPo was reduced by 87% ± 4% (at –100 mV) and 88% ± 6% (at +100 mV) after suppression of claudin-2 expression.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Events were rare in recordings from parental tight junctions.
source: Events were rare in recordings from parental tight junctions.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Voltage ramp recordings in claudin-2-expressing MDCKI monolayers show a linear current voltage relationship.
source: Representative recording of voltage ramp in claudin-2-expresing MDCKI monolayers showing linear current voltage relationship and reversal potential close to 0 mV.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Voltage ramp recordings in claudin-2-expressing MDCKI monolayers show a reversal potential close to 0 mV.
source: Representative recording of voltage ramp in claudin-2-expresing MDCKI monolayers showing linear current voltage relationship and reversal potential close to 0 mV.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Average channel conductance was ~90 pS regardless of whether claudin-2 expression was induced or not.
source: Average current voltage relationships (n = 8 to 32 per condition) reveals that average channel conductance was ~90 pS regardless of whether claudin-2 expression was induced (green line) or not (black line).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The reversal potential of claudin-2-dependent events is close to 0 mV, but slightly negative.
source: Current-voltage (I-V) relationship plots (Figure 2I,J) showed that the reversal potential (Vrev) of these events was close to 0 mV, but slightly negative, and followed a linear function of voltage, consistent with a passive process.
evidence: This is supported by voltage ramp data in Figure 2I,J.

claim: The current-voltage relationship of claudin-2-dependent events follows a linear function of voltage, consistent with a passive process.
source: Current-voltage (I-V) relationship plots (Figure 2I,J) showed that the reversal potential (Vrev) of these events was close to 0 mV, but slightly negative, and followed a linear function of voltage, consistent with a passive process.
evidence: This is supported by voltage ramp data in Figure 2I,J and is an inference about the nature of the process.

claim: The conductance events cannot be apical cation or anion channels because the extracellular:intracellular gradients of these ions would necessitate equilibrium potentials much different than 0 mV.
source: This result argues strongly that the conductance events cannot be apical cation or anion, e.g. K+, Na+, or Cl- channels, since the extracellular:intracellular gradients of these ions would necessitate equilibrium potentials much different than 0 mV.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reversal potential data and knowledge of ion gradients.

claim: Individual conductance events were quantitatively similar in both amplitude and duration when claudin-2 expression was low.
source: Notably, this analysis also shows that, despite there being far fewer events when claudin-2 expression was suppressed, individual conductance events were quantitatively similar, in both amplitude and duration, when claudin-2 expression was low (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 2J.

claim: The ~9 pA single channel conductances measured by trans-tight junction patch clamp are non-vectorial, as expected for passive paracellular channels.
source: Therefore, the ~9 pA single channel conductances measured by trans-tight junction patch clamp are non-vectorial, as expected for passive paracellular channels, and is unlikely be due to the activity of apical transmembrane ion channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the symmetrical behavior and reversal potential data.

claim: The ~9 pA single channel conductances are unlikely to be due to the activity of apical transmembrane ion channels.
source: Therefore, the ~9 pA single channel conductances measured by trans-tight junction patch clamp are non-vectorial, as expected for passive paracellular channels, and is unlikely be due to the activity of apical transmembrane ion channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on multiple lines of evidence including reversal potential and symmetry.

claim: Tight junction conductance has been assumed to be uniform over time.
source: The observation that claudin-2-dependent conductance events occur in bursts was somewhat surprising, as tight junction conductance has been assumed to be uniform over time.
evidence: This is a statement about the prevailing assumption in the field.

claim: The belief that tight junction conductance is uniform over time was based on stable measurements of paracellular conductance across large epithelial surfaces.
source: This widely-held belief was based on stable measurements of paracellular conductance across large epithelial surfaces.
evidence: This is an inference about why the field held this belief.

claim: Traditional measurements of paracellular conductance lack both temporal and spatial resolution.
source: However, conductance of individual channels is averaged over space in these measurements, which lack both temporal and spatial resolution of the trans-tight junction patch clamp approach.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of traditional methods.

claim: Opening duration histograms revealed a single population of openings with τopen< 1 ms.
source: Opening duration histograms of tight junction patch clamp data from cells with high or low claudin-2 expression at holding potentials of +100 or -100 mV. These revealed a single population of openings with τopen< 1 ms (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is supported by the histograms in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Closed duration histograms revealed two populations of closings, corresponding to closed states between and within event clusters.
source: In contrast, closed duration histograms under the same conditions revealed two populations of closings, corresponding to closed states between and within event clusters.
evidence: This is supported by the histograms in Figure 3E-H.

claim: Interburst closings were prolonged with τ closed(stable) >1 s.
source: Interburst closings were prolonged with τ closed(stable) >1 s while intraburst closings occurred with millisecond kinetics, i.e. τ closed(transient) < 2 ms (Figure 3E–H).
evidence: This is supported by the histograms in Figure 3E-H.

claim: Intraburst closings occurred with millisecond kinetics, i.e. τ closed(transient) < 2 ms.
source: Interburst closings were prolonged with τ closed(stable) >1 s while intraburst closings occurred with millisecond kinetics, i.e. τ closed(transient) < 2 ms (Figure 3E–H).
evidence: This is supported by the histograms in Figure 3E-H.

claim: The prolonged closed state (closedstable) could represent channel disassembly.
source: One possibility is that the prolonged state (closedstable) could represent channel disassembly, while the shorter closed state (closedtransient) results from regulation of assembled channels.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a possibility, representing speculation.

claim: The shorter closed state (closedtransient) could result from regulation of assembled channels.
source: One possibility is that the prolonged state (closedstable) could represent channel disassembly, while the shorter closed state (closedtransient) results from regulation of assembled channels.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a possibility, representing speculation.

claim: Claudin-2 protein has a ~9 hr half-life in MDCK monolayers.
source: However, given the absence of a significant vesicular claudin-2 pool and the relatively long ~9 hr half-life of claudin-2 protein in MDCK monolayers (Van Itallie et al., 2004), we consider it highly unlikely that vesicular traffic or protein turnover could be responsible for the observed opening and closing events.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Van Itallie et al., 2004.

claim: It is highly unlikely that vesicular traffic or protein turnover could be responsible for the observed opening and closing events.
source: However, given the absence of a significant vesicular claudin-2 pool and the relatively long ~9 hr half-life of claudin-2 protein in MDCK monolayers (Van Itallie et al., 2004), we consider it highly unlikely that vesicular traffic or protein turnover could be responsible for the observed opening and closing events.
evidence: This is an inference based on the protein half-life and absence of vesicular pools.

claim: The pool of claudin-2 at the tight junction is largely immobile.
source: In contrast, although the pool of claudin-2 at the tight junction is largely immobile (Raleigh et al., 2011), the limited intramembranous diffusion that does occur (Shen et al., 2008) has kinetics within the range of the longer closed state (closedstable) and we cannot exclude this as a possible regulatory mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Raleigh et al., 2011.

claim: Limited intramembranous diffusion of claudin-2 has kinetics within the range of the longer closed state (closedstable).
source: In contrast, although the pool of claudin-2 at the tight junction is largely immobile (Raleigh et al., 2011), the limited intramembranous diffusion that does occur (Shen et al., 2008) has kinetics within the range of the longer closed state (closedstable) and we cannot exclude this as a possible regulatory mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shen et al., 2008 and comparison with the measured kinetics.

claim: Intramembranous diffusion cannot be excluded as a possible regulatory mechanism for the longer closed state.
source: In contrast, although the pool of claudin-2 at the tight junction is largely immobile (Raleigh et al., 2011), the limited intramembranous diffusion that does occur (Shen et al., 2008) has kinetics within the range of the longer closed state (closedstable) and we cannot exclude this as a possible regulatory mechanism.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a possibility that cannot be excluded.

claim: Open and closed state kinetics were similar under high or low claudin-2 expression.
source: Similar to amplitude, open and closed state kinetics were similar under high or low claudin-2 expression.
evidence: This is supported by the kinetic analysis data in Figure 3I.

claim: Claudin-2 channel gating is independent of expression level, i.e. is non-cooperative.
source: Claudin-2 channel gating is thus independent of expression level, i.e. is non-cooperative.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity of kinetics at different expression levels.

claim: Changes in NPo that occur as a function of claudin-2 expression reflect differences in channel number rather than open probability of individual channels.
source: This also indicates that changes in NPo that occur as a function of claudin-2 expression reflect differences in channel number rather than open probability of individual channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that kinetics don't change with expression level.

claim: Claudin-2-dependent channels are not gated by voltage.
source: Further, because properties were similar at +100 and -100 mV, we can conclude that claudin-2-dependent channels are not gated by voltage, unlike many transmembrane ion channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity of properties at different voltages.

claim: Claudin-2-dependent channels can exist in a highly dynamic opening state (o) as well as stable (cstable) and transient (ctransient) closed states.
source: Overall these data show that claudin-2-dependent channels can exist in a highly dynamic opening state (o) as well as stable (cstable) and transient (ctransient) closed states (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is a summary of the kinetic analysis data.

claim: The ~9 pA claudin-2-dependent openings were never observed when electrodes were sealed off of the tight junction.
source: The ~9 pA claudin-2-dependent openings were, however, never observed when electrodes were sealed off of the tight junction, i.e. over apical membranes away from the tight junction.
evidence: This is a statement about the spatial specificity of the recordings.

claim: Small conductances could sometimes be detected when electrodes were sealed over apical membranes, but only when the data were low-pass filtered at 500 Hz.
source: In place of the ~9 pA openings, small conductances could sometimes be detected when electrodes were sealed over apical membranes, but only when the data were low-pass filtered at 500 Hz (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Small conductances detected over apical membranes were more common at holding potentials of +100 mV, relative to -100 mV.
source: These events differed distinctly from the claudin-2-dependent conducances, as the former were more common at holding potentials of +100 mV, relative to -100 mV, and had amplitudes of less than 2 pA, well below those of claudin-2-dependent events.
evidence: This is based on analysis of off-tight junction recordings.

claim: Small conductances detected over apical membranes had amplitudes of less than 2 pA, well below those of claudin-2-dependent events.
source: These events differed distinctly from the claudin-2-dependent conducances, as the former were more common at holding potentials of +100 mV, relative to -100 mV, and had amplitudes of less than 2 pA, well below those of claudin-2-dependent events.
evidence: This is based on analysis of off-tight junction recordings.

claim: The spatial specificity of recordings provides evidence that the conductances detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp are not traditional, transmembrane apical ion channels.
source: These data provide spatial evidence that the conductances detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp are not traditional, transmembrane apical ion channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the spatial distribution of different conductance events.

claim: Events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp were not blocked by three different ion channel inhibitor cocktails.
source: Events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp were not blocked by three different ion channel inhibitor cocktails (+Cldn-2; representative of n = 3 to 8 per condition).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The number of events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp was reduced at 15°C, relative to 37°C.
source: The number of events detected was reduced at 15°C, relative to 37°C, but event amplitude was unaffected (+Cldn-2; representative of n = 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Event amplitude was unaffected by cooling to 15°C.
source: The number of events detected was reduced at 15°C, relative to 37°C, but event amplitude was unaffected (+Cldn-2; representative of n = 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: NPo and Na+ permeability measured across a 0.33 cm2 monolayer were similarly reduced at 15°C.
source: NPo and Na+ permeability measured across a 0.33 cm2 monolayer were similarly reduced at 15°C (+Cldn-2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D.

claim: When monolayers of claudin-2-expressing MDCKI were cooled from 37°C to 15°C while recording, the number of claudin-2-dependent (~9 pA) events fell by 37%.
source: When monolayers of claudin-2-expressing MDCKI were cooled from 37°C to 15°C while recording, the number of claudin-2-dependent (~9 pA) events fell by 37% (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The 37% decrease in claudin-2-dependent events upon cooling was closely paralleled by a 41% decrease in Na+ permeability measured across monolayers using traditional approaches.
source: This was closely paralleled by a 41% decrease in Na+ permeability measured across monolayers using traditional approaches (Figure 4D), providing more support for the conclusion that the ~9 pA conductance events reflect activity of paracellular claudin-2 channels.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D and supports the conclusion about the nature of the events.

claim: The ~4 pA events were resistant to cold, even when chilled to 10°C.
source: In contrast to the ~9 pA events, the ~4 pA events were resistant to cold (p = 0.35), even when chilled to 10°C (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The ~4 pA events were resistant to all of the ion channel inhibitor cocktails.
source: The ~4 pA events were also resistant to all of the ion channel inhibitor cocktails (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4F.

claim: MDCK cell line is derived from epithelia of the distal convoluted tubule.
source: The MDCK cell line is derived from epithelia of the distal convoluted tubule, which function effectively to absorb Na+ and Cl- in the apical-to-basal direction and secrete K+ (Gekle et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gekle et al., 1994.

claim: Distal convoluted tubule epithelia function effectively to absorb Na+ and Cl- in the apical-to-basal direction and secrete K+.
source: The MDCK cell line is derived from epithelia of the distal convoluted tubule, which function effectively to absorb Na+ and Cl- in the apical-to-basal direction and secrete K+ (Gekle et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gekle et al., 1994.

claim: Caco-2 cells are a human colon epithelial cancer cell line that differentiate as absorptive enterocytes.
source: For example, Caco-2 cells are a human colon epithelial cancer cell line that differentiate as absorptive enterocytes and express brush border enzymes and transporters typical of this cell type (Peterson and Mooseker, 1992, Pinto et al., 1983, Turner and Black, 2001, Turner et al., 1996, Turner et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Caco-2 cells express brush border enzymes and transporters typical of absorptive enterocytes.
source: For example, Caco-2 cells are a human colon epithelial cancer cell line that differentiate as absorptive enterocytes and express brush border enzymes and transporters typical of this cell type (Peterson and Mooseker, 1992, Pinto et al., 1983, Turner and Black, 2001, Turner et al., 1996, Turner et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Tight junction ultrastructure is similar in MDCK and Caco-2 cells, and both are composed of three to five strands.
source: Nevertheless, tight junction ultrastructure is similar in MDCK and Caco-2 cells, and both are composed of three to five strands (Figure 5A), which express claudin-2 abundantly (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Both MDCK and Caco-2 cells express claudin-2 abundantly.
source: Nevertheless, tight junction ultrastructure is similar in MDCK and Caco-2 cells, and both are composed of three to five strands (Figure 5A), which express claudin-2 abundantly (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: Paracellular Na+ conductance across Caco-2BBe monolayers was similar to that of MDCKI monolayers with induced claudin-2 expression.
source: Paracellular Na+ conductance across Caco-2BBe monolayers was similar to that of MDCKI monolayers with induced claudin-2 expression (Figure 5D vs Figure 1F).
evidence: This is shown by comparing Figures 5D and 1F.

claim: When claudin-2 expression was stably suppressed by shRNA-mediated knockdown, Na+ conductance across Caco-2BBe monolayers was greatly diminished.
source: When claudin-2 expression was stably suppressed by shRNA-mediated knockdown, Na+ conductance across Caco-2BBe monolayers was greatly diminished (Figure 5D) and fell to a level similar to the claudin-2-deficient MDCKI parental line (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5D.

claim: All points histograms of Caco-2BBe cells demonstrate conductance values centered around ~8 pA, i.e. ~82 pS, in claudin-2-expressing monolayers.
source: As with MDCK monolayers, all points histograms demonstrate conductance values centered around ~8 pA, i.e. ~82 pS, in claudin-2-expressing monolayers (Figure 5F), and there was a specific reduction in this class of events after claudin-2 knockdown (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5F.

claim: There was a specific reduction in ~8 pA events after claudin-2 knockdown in Caco-2BBe cells.
source: As with MDCK monolayers, all points histograms demonstrate conductance values centered around ~8 pA, i.e. ~82 pS, in claudin-2-expressing monolayers (Figure 5F), and there was a specific reduction in this class of events after claudin-2 knockdown (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Claudin-2 depletion in human intestinal epithelia eliminates events similar to those generated by claudin-2 expression in canine renal epithelia.
source: We therefore conclude that claudin-2 depletion in human intestinal epithelia eliminates events similar to those generated by claudin-2 expression in canine renal epithelia.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of MDCK and Caco-2 data.

claim: NPo was reduced by claudin-2 knockdown in Caco-2BBe cells, but conductance of the claudin-2-dependent events was not affected.
source: While NPo was reduced, conductance of the claudin-2-dependent events was not affected by claudin-2-knockdown (Figure 5H), demonstrating that single channel conductance was not a function of claudin-2 concentration.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Single channel conductance was not a function of claudin-2 concentration.
source: While NPo was reduced, conductance of the claudin-2-dependent events was not affected by claudin-2-knockdown (Figure 5H), demonstrating that single channel conductance was not a function of claudin-2 concentration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that conductance doesn't change with expression level.

claim: Gating of claudin-2-dependent channels is not cooperative.
source: Similar to the data from MDCK monolayers, this indicates that gating of claudin-2-dependent channels is not cooperative.
evidence: This is an inference based on the independence of gating from expression level.

claim: A class of smaller conductances that were not affected by claudin-2 knockdown was also detected in Caco-2BBe cells.
source: A class of smaller conductances that were not affected by claudin-2 knockdown was also detected, similar to the claudin-2-independent events detected in MDCK monolayers.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the patch clamp data from Caco-2 cells.

claim: The claudin-2-dependent openings were not detectable when the patch pipette was sealed away from the tight junction in Caco-2BBe monolayers.
source: Finally, as in MDCK cells, the claudin-2-dependent openings were not detectable when the patch pipette was sealed away from the tight junction in Caco-2BBe monolayers (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Tight junction opening events are detectable in two very different epithelia derived from different organ systems.
source: Thus, these data demonstrate the tight junction opening events are detectable in two very different epithelia derived from different organ systems, and, in both cases, the events were claudin-2 dependent.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings from both MDCK and Caco-2 cells.

claim: The events detected in both MDCK and Caco-2 cells were claudin-2 dependent.
source: Thus, these data demonstrate the tight junction opening events are detectable in two very different epithelia derived from different organ systems, and, in both cases, the events were claudin-2 dependent.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings from both cell types.

claim: The data exclude the possibility that events could be due to off-target effects induced by the tet transactivator used to drive claudin-2 expression in MDCK cells.
source: Further, these data exclude the possibility that events could be due to off-target effects induced by the tet transactivator used to drive claudin-2 expression in MDCK cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of similar events in Caco-2 cells without the tet system.

claim: The similar conductance values of events in MDCK and Caco-2 cells, despite markedly different NPo values, supports the conclusion that the events are mediated by biophysically similar claudin-2-based paracellular channels.
source: More importantly, the similar conductance values of these events, despite markedly different NPo values, supports the conclusion that the events are mediated by biophysically similar claudin-2-based paracellular channels, rather than some other paracellular channel that might be expected to differ between canine renal and human intestinal epithelia.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of conductance and NPo values across cell types.

claim: Paracellular flux across tight junction channels is driven passively by transepithelial electrochemical gradients.
source: Paracellular flux across tight junction channels is driven passively by transepithelial electrochemical gradients.
evidence: This is established knowledge about paracellular transport.

claim: Similar shifts in reversal potential but in opposite directions were observed by iso-osmotically replacing 90% of basolateral or apical NaCl with mannitol.
source: As predicted for a paracellular conductive pathway, we observed similar shifts in reversal potential but in opposite directions by iso-osmotically replacing 90% of basolateral or apical NaCl with mannitol (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: The symmetrical behavior of reversal potential shifts indicates that flux across these channels is electrochemically driven by apical:basolateral gradients.
source: Importantly, such symmetrical behavior indicates that flux across these channels is electrochemically driven by apical:basolateral gradients.
evidence: This is an inference based on the symmetrical reversal potential shifts.

claim: Transmembrane ion channels are driven by extracellular:intracellular gradients.
source: In contrast, transmembrane ion channels are driven by extracellular:intracellular gradients.
evidence: This is established knowledge about transmembrane ion channels.

claim: Transmembrane ion channels would not be expected to behave symmetrically under conditions where extracellular media is changed rapidly.
source: As intracellular cation composition does not change as rapidly as the extracellular media, transmembrane ion channels would not be expected to behave symmetrically under these conditions.
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge of how transmembrane channels respond to gradients.

claim: The PNa+/PCl− of single channel events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp is 7.4 ± 3.7.
source: The magnitude of reversal potential shifts indicates that the PNa+/PCl−, as defined by Nernst equilibrium potentials, of single channel events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp is 7.4 ± 3.7.
evidence: This is calculated from the reversal potential data.

claim: The PNa+/PCl− measured across intact monolayers using traditional global measurement approaches is 9.5 ± 0.1.
source: This is similar to the PNa+/PCl− of 9.5 ± 0.1 measured across intact monolayers using traditional global measurement approaches (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The detected single channel events have PNa+/PCl− that is indistinguishable from that of tight junctions measured by traditional methods.
source: In addition to demonstrating that the detected single channel events have PNa+/PCl− that is indistinguishable from that of tight junctions, these data also exclude the possibility that openings represent anion channels, such as CFTR, that would be expected to be Cl-, rather than Na+, selective.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of PNa+/PCl− values.

claim: The reversal potential data exclude the possibility that openings represent anion channels, such as CFTR.
source: In addition to demonstrating that the detected single channel events have PNa+/PCl− that is indistinguishable from that of tight junctions, these data also exclude the possibility that openings represent anion channels, such as CFTR, that would be expected to be Cl-, rather than Na+, selective.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cation selectivity demonstrated by the reversal potential data.

claim: Paracellular tight junction permeability is well recognized to be size-selective.
source: When measured across intact monolayers, paracellular tight junction permeability is well recognized to be size-selective.
evidence: This is established knowledge about tight junction permeability.

claim: The channels detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp were permeable to methylamine (radius=1.9 Å).
source: Use of the trans-tight junction patch clamp in conjunction with biionic substitution showed that the channels were permeable to methylamine (radius=1.9 Å) and that, like Na+, the Vrev of methylamine was close to 0 mV (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The Vrev of methylamine was close to 0 mV, indicating that conductance of Na+ and methylamine is similar in magnitude.
source: Use of the trans-tight junction patch clamp in conjunction with biionic substitution showed that the channels were permeable to methylamine (radius=1.9 Å) and that, like Na+, the Vrev of methylamine was close to 0 mV (Figure 6C). This indicates that conductance of Na+ and methylamine is similar in magnitude.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reversal potential data in Figure 6C.

claim: Channels detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp were relatively impermeant to tetramethylammonium (radius=2.8 Å) and N-methyl-D-glucamine (radius=3.6 Å).
source: In contrast, channels detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp were relatively impermeant to the larger cations tetramethylammonium (radius=2.8 Å) and N-methyl-D-glucamine (radius=3.6 Å).
evidence: This is supported by the reversal potential data in Figures 6D-F.

claim: Basolateral Na+ replacement with tetramethylammonium or N-methyl-D-glucamine induced a large negative shift in channel reversal.
source: Thus, basolateral Na+ replacement with these larger cations induced a large negative shift in channel reversal (Figure 6D–F).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 6D-F.

claim: Global analyses of claudin-2-expressing MDCK by biionic substitution demonstrated tight junction size-selectivity that paralleled that of conductance events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp.
source: Global analyses of claudin-2-expressing MDCK by biionic substitution demonstrated tight junction size-selectivity that paralleled that of conductance events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The size-selectivity data provide further support that the events detected cannot represent apical K+ channels, as the latter are highly-selective and do not accommodate cations as large as methylamine.
source: In addition to providing another biophysical measure in which the claudin-2-dependent events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp are similar to claudin-2-dependent paracellular conductances measured by traditional averaging approaches, these data provide further support for the conclusion that the events detected cannot represent apical K+ channels, as the latter are highly-selective and do not accommodate cations as large as methylamine.
evidence: This is an inference based on the size-selectivity data and knowledge of K+ channel properties.

claim: The permeability of methylamine, relative to Na+, is greater in patch clamp measurements than in global measurements.
source: It is, however, interesting to note that the permeability of methylamine, relative to Na+, is greater in patch clamp measurements than in global measurements.
evidence: This is an observation based on comparison of data in Figures 6G.

claim: The claudin-2 dependent channel represents a passive paracellular conductance pathway with charge- and size-selectivities similar to those measured across large epithelial sheets.
source: These data therefore demonstrate that the claudin-2 dependent channel represents a passive paracellular conductance pathway with charge- and size-selectivities similar to those measured across large epithelial sheets.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the selectivity data.

claim: La3+ is known to nonspecifically inhibit claudin-2-dependent paracellular flux.
source: La3+ is known to nonspecifically inhibit claudin-2-dependent paracellular flux (Machen et al., 1972, Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Addition of La3+ to the basolateral chamber completely blocked claudin-2 dependent opening events.
source: Consistent with this, addition of La3+ to the basolateral chamber completely blocked claudin-2 dependent opening events (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 7A-C.

claim: The La3+ data, along with the ionic substitution experiments, indicate that the channels being studied are equally accessible from apical and basolateral approaches.
source: These data, along with the ionic substitution experiments above, indicate that the channels being studied are equally accessible from apical and basolateral approaches and again refute hypotheses suggesting that the openings detected represent plasma membrane ion channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the La3+ blocking data and ionic substitution experiments.

claim: Ile66 within claudin-2 is thought to be buried within a narrow part of the channel.
source: Within the corresponding region of claudin-2, Ile66 is thought to be buried within a narrow part of the channel (Angelow and Yu, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Angelow and Yu, 2009.

claim: Covalent modification of claudin-2I66C using MTSET reduced global paracellular cation flux in claudin-2I66C, but not claudin-2WT.
source: Covalent modification of claudin-2I66C using 2-(trimethylammonium) ethyl methanethiosulfonate (MTSET) reduced global paracellular cation flux in claudin-2I66C, but not claudin-2WT, consistent with obstruction of the claudin-2 pore (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7D and is consistent with previous work.

claim: MTSET markedly reduced NPo of MDCKI monolayers expressing claudin-2I66C.
source: Trans-tight junction patch clamp recordings demonstrated that MTSET markedly reduced NPo of MDCKI monolayers expressing claudin-2I66C (Figure 7F,H,J) with kinetics similar to MTSET inhibition measured by global approaches (Angelow and Yu, 2009).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 7F, H, and J.

claim: MTSET had no effect on channel events in monolayers expressing claudin-2WT.
source: As expected, MTSET had no effect on channel events in monolayers expressing claudin-2WT(Figure 7G,I).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 7G and I.

claim: In most cases, MTSET completely abolished events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp in monolayers expressing claudin-2I66C.
source: In most cases, MTSET completely abolished events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp in monolayers expressing claudin-2I66C (Figure 7H), but a few residual events persisted in some monolayers (Figure 7H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7H.

claim: MTSET-resistant events were identical in size to those observed prior to MTSET addition.
source: These MTSET-resistant events were identical in size to those observed prior to MTSET addition (Figure 7J), suggesting that MTSET inhibits each claudin-2 channel either completely or not at all.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7J and leads to an inference about the mechanism of inhibition.

claim: MTSET inhibits each claudin-2 channel either completely or not at all.
source: These MTSET-resistant events were identical in size to those observed prior to MTSET addition (Figure 7J), suggesting that MTSET inhibits each claudin-2 channel either completely or not at all.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that residual events have the same amplitude.

claim: Site-directed mutagenesis and chemical derivatization of Ile66 blocks local conductance events in a specific manner.
source: In either case, these data show that site-directed mutagenesis and chemical derivatization of Ile66 blocks local conductance events in a specific manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the MTSET experiments.

claim: Claudin-2 is concentrated at the tight junction.
source: Because claudin-2 is concentrated at the tight junction and has not been demonstrated to create transmembrane channels, this result provides further support for the conclusion that events represent flux across paracellular, i.e. tight junction, channels.
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence data (Figure 1C, 5C) and established knowledge.

claim: Claudin-2 has not been demonstrated to create transmembrane channels.
source: Because claudin-2 is concentrated at the tight junction and has not been demonstrated to create transmembrane channels, this result provides further support for the conclusion that events represent flux across paracellular, i.e. tight junction, channels.
evidence: This is a statement about the lack of evidence for transmembrane claudin-2 channels.

claim: The biophysical behavior of claudin-2-dependent single channel conductance events has been defined in both canine kidney and human intestinal epithelia.
source: We have defined the biophysical behavior of claudin-2-dependent single channel conductance events in both canine kidney and human intestinal epithelia.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: Claudin-2 channels within tight junctions are driven passively by the transepithelial, apical to basolateral electrochemical gradient.
source: The data confirm that claudin-2 channels within tight junctions are driven passively by the transepithelial, apical to basolateral electrochemical gradient.
evidence: This is confirmed by the symmetrical behavior and reversal potential data.

claim: The single channel size- and charge-selectivity of claudin-2 channels is nearly identical to values obtained when the same parameters are assessed across large epithelial sheets using traditional methods.
source: Analyses of single channel events show that the single channel size- and charge-selectivity of these channels is nearly identical to values obtained when the same parameters are assessed across large epithelial sheets using traditional methods.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of patch clamp and traditional measurements (Figures 1, 6).

claim: Single channel events were inhibited by La3+, reduced temperature, and cysteine mutagenesis and chemical derivitization of Ile66 within the claudin-2 pore.
source: Further, single channel events were inhibited by La3+, reduced temperature, and, more specifically, cysteine mutagenesis and chemical derivitization of Ile66 within the claudin-2 pore.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 4 and 7.

claim: Attempts to block single claudin-2 openings with numerous established transmembrane ion channel blockers were unsuccessful.
source: In contrast, attempts to block single claudin-2 openings with numerous established transmembrane ion channel blockers were unsuccessful.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: The symmetrical behavior and size-selectivity of the claudin-2-dependent events are inconsistent with known and predicted transmembrane ion channels.
source: Moreover, the symmetrical behavior and size-selectivity of the claudin-2-dependent events detected by trans-tight junction patch clamp are inconsistent with known and predicted transmembrane, e.g. apical or basolateral membrane, ion channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with known properties of transmembrane channels.

claim: The conductance events detected represent opening and closing of trans-tight junction channels.
source: Thus, we must conclude that the conductance events detected do represent opening and closing of trans-tight junction channels.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, based on all the evidence presented.

claim: Trans-tight junction flux occurs via highly dynamic, rather than static, paracellular channels that are gated with sub-millisecond kinetics.
source: It is, perhaps, surprising that trans-tight junction flux occurs via highly dynamic, rather than static, paracellular channels that are gated with sub-millisecond kinetics.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the kinetic analysis data.

claim: Paracellular channels open and close in a manner similar to typical ion channels that span the plasma membrane, despite being oriented parallel to the plasma membrane.
source: This suggests that, despite being oriented parallel to, rather than across, the plasma membrane, paracellular channels open and close in a manner similar to typical ion channels that span the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gating behavior observed.

claim: Claudins do not have any sequence similarity to known transmembrane ion channels.
source: Claudins do not, however, have any sequence similarity to known transmembrane ion channels.
evidence: This is a statement based on knowledge of claudin and ion channel sequences.

claim: Claudin-dependent tight junction channels represent an entirely new class of dynamically gated ion conductance pathways.
source: Thus, claudin-dependent tight junction channels represent an entirely new class of dynamically gated ion conductance pathways.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the novelty of the findings and the lack of sequence similarity to known channels.

claim: Tight junction ultrastructure is established by an anastomosing arrangement of strands which encircle the cell at the apical intercellular space.
source: Tight junction ultrastructure, as seen using freeze-fracture electron microscopy, is established by an anastomosing arrangement of strands which encircle the cell at the apical intercellular space.
evidence: This is established knowledge about tight junction structure.

claim: It has been proposed that tight junction strands establish the paracellular barrier and are populated by channels which impart charge and size selectivity.
source: It has been proposed that these strands establish the paracellular barrier and that the strands are also populated by "channels" which impart charge and size selectivity.
evidence: This is a statement about a prevailing model in the field.

claim: Whether tight junction channels are open at steady state or can open and close was previously unknown.
source: Whether these channels, commonly referred to as the pore pathway (Shen et al., 2011), are open at steady state or can open and close was previously unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge before this study.

claim: Tight junctions are populated by highly dynamic, gated channels that transition between at least three different states.
source: Our data show that tight junctions are populated by highly dynamic, gated channels that transition between at least three different states.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the kinetic analysis data.

claim: Any model of claudin channel function based on the crystal structure of claudin-15 must include an explanation for rapid opening and closing of the channel.
source: Further, as investigators in this area seek to model claudin channel function based on the published crystal structure of claudin-15 (Suzuki et al., 2014), our data indicate that any model applied to claudin-2 must include an explanation for rapid opening and closing of the channel.
evidence: This is an implication of the findings for future structural modeling work.

claim: The longer closed state may reflect transient disassembly of the claudin-2 channel complex.
source: One could hypothesize that, in contrast to the shorter closed state, the longer closed state may reflect transient disassembly of the claudin-2 channel complex.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a hypothesis, representing speculation.

claim: Some of the properties observed in single channel recordings are due to the arrangement of channels spanning tight junction strands that are oriented in both series and parallel.
source: We speculate that some of the properties observed in our single channel recordings are due to the arrangement of channels spanning tight junction strands that are oriented in both series and parallel, implying that multiple simultaneous tight junction channel openings would result in stepwise conductance increases.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: Short-lived, step-wise conductance increases were observed, consistent with a parallel opening of a second claudin-2 channel.
source: Indeed, we did observe short-lived, step-wise conductance increases, consistent with a parallel opening of a second claudin-2 channel, superimposed on a typical initial opening (e.g., Figures 4B,6B,E and 7G).
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: The multi-strand tight junction ultrastructure suggests that channels are arranged in series.
source: Alternatively, the multi-strand tight junction ultrastructure and corresponding conductance model proposed by Claude (Claude, 1978) suggest that channels are also arranged in series.
evidence: This is based on citation to Claude, 1978 and structural knowledge.

claim: If channels are arranged in series, the NPo measured for current across the entire height of the tight junction significantly underestimates the NPo of individual claudin-2 channels.
source: If true, this would indicate that the NPo measured here for current across the entire height of the tight junction significantly underestimates the NPo of individual claudin-2 channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the series arrangement hypothesis.

claim: Some variability in claudin-2-dependent current amplitude was observed.
source: Consistent with this, we did observed some variability in claudin-2-dependent current amplitude.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: Heterogeneity in current amplitude may be due to variations in baseline strand conductance, different numbers of tight junction strands, or variations in strand branch points within a particular patch of tight junction.
source: This could be related to the specific configuration of a claudin-2 channel within a given submicron segment of tight junction. For example, heterogeneity may be due to variations in baseline strand conductance, different numbers of tight junction strands, or variations in strand branch points within a particular patch of tight junction.
evidence: This is speculation about possible explanations for the observed variability.

claim: The anastamosing arrangement of tight junction strands may be a mechanism that limits lateral spread of current from single channel openings within any individual strand.
source: Indeed, the anastamosing arrangement of tight junction strands may be a mechanism that limits lateral spread of current from single channel openings within any individual strand.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional significance of tight junction structure.

claim: When the pipette was in solution, free of cells, the resistance was determined to be 2.5 MΩ.
source: First, we determined resistance of the patch pipette electrode itself. When in solution, i.e. free of cells, the resistance was determined to be 2.5 MΩ, similar to that of electrode used by others.
evidence: This is a measurement of electrode resistance.

claim: When the pipette was sealed to the monolayer, resistance of the seal leak was determined to be ~30 GΩ.
source: When the pipette was sealed to the monolayer, resistance of the seal leak, i.e. the path resulting from incomplete electrical isolation at the edges of the pipette, was determined to be ~30 GΩ, based on the steady-state current of (~3.5 pA) at -100 mV when the pipette was sealed over the junction of claudin-2-deficient monolayers composed of either parental or uninduced, transfected MDCKI cells.
evidence: This is calculated from the steady-state current in claudin-2-deficient cells.

claim: The resistance of the paracellular shunt pathway (outside of the pipette) ranged from 100 to 1,500 Ω·cm2, i.e. 0.0003 to 0.0045 MΩ.
source: The resistance of the paracellular shunt pathway (outside of the pipette) is simply the measured resistance of the monolayer, which ranged from 100 to 1,500 Ω·cm2, i.e. 0.0003 to 0.0045 MΩ.
evidence: This is based on TER measurements.

claim: After accounting for low pipette seal leak and electrode resistance, the conductance events detected by the patch pipette can only represent transepithelial currents.
source: Thus, after accounting for low pipette seal leak and electrode resistance, the conductance events detected by the patch pipette can only represent transepithelial currents.
evidence: This is an inference based on the equivalent circuit analysis.

claim: When the pipette was sealed over the apical membrane away from the junction, ~2 pA currents could be detected at 100 mV, which corresponds to a pathway with a resistance of 50 GΩ.
source: To specifically assess non-tight junction conductance pathways that could, for example, be due to apical membrane trapped within the patch pipette, the pipette was sealed over the apical membrane, i.e. away from the junction. In this configuration, ~2 pA currents could be detected at 100 mV, which corresponds to a pathway with a resistance of 50 GΩ.
evidence: This is based on off-tight junction recordings.

claim: The ~9 pA events were present only when the pipette was sealed over the junction.
source: Two additional pathways, measuring ~9 pA and ~4 pA events were present only when the pipette was sealed over the junction.
evidence: This is based on comparison of on-junction and off-junction recordings.

claim: The ~4 pA events were present only when the pipette was sealed over the junction.
source: Two additional pathways, measuring ~9 pA and ~4 pA events were present only when the pipette was sealed over the junction.
evidence: This is based on comparison of on-junction and off-junction recordings.

claim: The ~9 pA events were absent in cells devoid of claudin-2, i.e. the parental MDCKI line.
source: The ~9 pA at 100 mV, or 11 GΩ, events were present in MDCKI or Caco-2BBe cells expressing both high and low levels of claudin-2, but were absent in cells devoid of claudin-2, i.e. the parental MDCKI line.
evidence: This is based on recordings from parental MDCKI cells.

claim: The frequency of detection of ~9 pA events correlated with claudin-2 expression indicating that these events are strictly claudin-2 dependent.
source: The frequency of detection correlated with claudin-2 expression indicating that these events are strictly claudin-2 dependent.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between expression and event frequency.

claim: The ~4 pA events were detected in the presence or absence of claudin-2 expression.
source: In contrast, the ~4 pA at 100 mV, or 25 GΩ, events were detected in the presence or absence of claudin-2 expression.
evidence: This is based on recordings from cells with and without claudin-2.

claim: The ~4 pA events may represent a paracellular channel that accounts for the electrical conductance measured across sheets of claudin-2-deficient cells using traditional methods.
source: At this point, we cannot define these events as due to a specific protein or channel. However, they are only detected at the tight junction and may, therefore represent a paracellular, i.e. tight junction, channel that accounts for the electrical conductance measured across sheets of claudin-2-deficient cells using traditional methods.
evidence: This is speculation about the nature of the ~4 pA events.

claim: In addition to the claudin-dependent size- and charge-selective pore pathway, a charge non-selective leak pathway that allows paracellular flux of small and large molecules is also present.
source: In addition to the claudin-dependent size- and charge-selective pore pathway, a charge non-selective leak pathway that allows paracellular flux of small and large molecules is also present (Anderson and Van Itallie, 2009, Turner, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Occludin and ZO-1 are both important to leak pathway regulation.
source: We and others have shown that occludin- and ZO-1 are both important to leak pathway regulation (Buschmann et al., 2013, Van Itallie et al., 2009) and that, in the intestine, increased leak pathway permeability is induced by TNF via a myosin light chain kinase-dependent process (Buschmann et al., 2013, Clayburgh et al., 2005, Van Itallie et al., 2010, Zolotarevsky et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In the intestine, increased leak pathway permeability is induced by TNF via a myosin light chain kinase-dependent process.
source: We and others have shown that occludin- and ZO-1 are both important to leak pathway regulation (Buschmann et al., 2013, Van Itallie et al., 2009) and that, in the intestine, increased leak pathway permeability is induced by TNF via a myosin light chain kinase-dependent process (Buschmann et al., 2013, Clayburgh et al., 2005, Van Itallie et al., 2010, Zolotarevsky et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The leak pathway may have an effective radius of 62.5 Å.
source: Our in vitro studies suggest that this pathway may have an effective radius of 62.5 Å (Buschmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Buschmann et al., 2013.

claim: A defined population of very large openings was not detected in any patch clamp recordings.
source: We did not, however, detect a defined population of very large openings in any of our patch clamp recordings.
evidence: This is a statement about what was not observed in the data.

claim: The leak pathway has limited or no dynamic gating, is extremely rare, or cannot be distinguished from electrode seal loss.
source: This suggests that the leak pathway has limited or no dynamic gating, are extremely rare, or cannot be distinguished from electrode seal loss.
evidence: This is speculation about why large openings were not detected.

claim: Some investigators have proposed that the leak pathway opens as one tight junction strand at a time, with materials trapped between strands until the next channel opens.
source: Alternatively, some investigators have proposed that the leak pathway opens as one tight junction strand at a time, with materials trapped between strands until the next channel opens (Sasaki et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sasaki et al., 2003.

claim: It has been suggested that leak pathway flux occurs primarily at tricellular tight junctions.
source: It has also been suggested that leak pathway flux occurs primarily at tricellular tight junctions.
evidence: This is a statement about a hypothesis in the field.

claim: The geometry or small size of tricellular contacts makes it exceedingly difficult to place and seal an electrode.
source: We therefore attempted to seal patch pipettes over tricellular contacts. Unfortunately, either the geometry or small size of these regions makes it exceedingly difficult to place and seal an electrode.
evidence: This is a statement about technical challenges encountered.

claim: Either a significant technical revision to the trans-tight junction patch clamp or completely different approaches will be required to perform single channel analyses of the leak pathway or tricellular tight junction.
source: We therefore conclude that either a significant technical revision to our trans-tight junction patch clamp or completely different approaches will be required to perform single channel analyses of the leak pathway or tricellular tight junction.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the limitations of the current technique.

claim: Trans-tight junction patch clamp recordings reveal sub-millisecond timescale gating of single paracellular channels that define trans-tight junction, paracellular conductance.
source: In summary, our novel trans-tight junction patch clamp recordings reveal sub-millisecond timescale gating of single paracellular channels that define trans-tight junction, paracellular conductance.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings.

claim: The channels depicted bridge two extracellular compartments, lumen and tissue, and represent an entirely new class of gated ion channels.
source: Unlike conventional transmembrane ion channels, which regulate flux between extracellular and intracellular compartments, the channels depicted here bridge two extracellular compartments, lumen and tissue, and, therefore, represent an entirely new class of gated ion channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the novelty of the findings.

claim: The ability to detect individual conductance events will be a critical tool in determination of molecular mechanisms that regulate channel assembly and gating.
source: Together with mutagenesis and structural analyses, the ability to detect individual conductance events, as described here, will be a critical tool in determination of molecular mechanisms that regulate channel assembly and gating.
evidence: This is a statement about the future utility of the technique.

claim: Studies using trans-tight junction patch clamp may lead to development of pharmacological means of modulating gating activity for therapeutic purposes.
source: Such studies may lead to development of pharmacological means of modulating gating activity for therapeutic purposes.
evidence: This is speculation about potential therapeutic applications.
